claims.claim: 2026 income tax brackets on active income (מיגיעה אישית), per the ITA monthly deductions booklet: 10% to 84,120; 14% to 120,720; 20% to 228,000; 31% to 301,200; 35% to 560,280; 47% on every additional shekel. The 47% band does not end at the surtax threshold. Brackets 3-5 were widened by the Economic Efficiency Law 2026, chapter C, effective 1 January 2026.

Each credit point (nekudat zikui) reduces annual tax by 2,904 NIS (242/month, frozen 2025-2027). Category values: resident male 2.25, female 2.75, new immigrant 3.0/2.0/1.0, child born 1.5, child 1-5 = 2.5, child 6-17 = 1.0, child 18 = 0.5, single parent 1.0, BA/vocational 1.0, MA 0.5, disability 2.0, combat reserve 0.5-1.0 The booklet states only the monthly credit-point value (242 per month, section 33A); the annual 2,904 figure is 242 x 12 and the per-category counts come from the Income Tax Ordinance, not from this booklet.

claims.claim: Section 17(11) of the Income Tax Ordinance allows deduction of expenses for preparing the return(s) and handling the tax matter in all assessment (shuma) and appeal (irur) proceedings, including CPA/tax-advisor fees and representation before the pakid shuma. Available to BOTH salaried employees and self-employed; the only statutory carve-out is business/profession income where no books (pinkasim) were kept, which does not affect salaried filers. Legal expenses on a frivolous objection/appeal are disallowed and awarded costs reduce the claim. Form 1301 has no dedicated field for a salaried filer's 17(11) deduction (field 158 is the gross-salary line, cross-checked against Form 106)
